notes: This scenario intentionally asks for structured output so captured reports can be scored offline.
Run it through the plugin/model surface you want to evaluate, not through a direct API harness.

reviewPacket.goal: Run a focused architecture and regression audit of Flow review prompting quality without executing code.
architecture: Standalone /flow-review prompt -> audit contract -> review report schema -> renderer.
Review capture scenario -> generated prompt packet -> prompt behavior eval scoring.

excluded: Runtime session execution internals except where they shape final-review evidence semantics.
Release automation unless it directly changes review prompt capture behavior.

relationships: Prompt input packet sections must survive into review coverage notes and finding scope.
Structured ledger validation should complement, not replace, packet-boundary preservation.
ambiguities: If a requested surface is not present in the selected context, record the gap instead of inventing evidence.
Distinguish prompt-contract ambiguity from a confirmed runtime defect.
knownExclusions: Do not audit package-manager detection or install lifecycle unless new evidence links it to review prompting.
alreadyCoveredFindings: Do not repeat generic full-audit overclaim findings unless the packet boundary creates a larger blocker.
evidenceRequirements: Use concrete first-party path:line references for directly reviewed files.
Use coverageNotes for exclusions, ambiguities, and relationship paths that constrain the review.
doneWhen: The output preserves selected-context limits and known exclusions.
Findings are ordered by severity and do not duplicate already-covered findings without new evidence.

notes: This scenario forces connected-context accounting from an async/action entrypoint.
A review that only claims changed files were reviewed should fail packet-boundary scoring.

reviewPacket.goal: Verify review coverage does not collapse to changed files only when async action edges imply broader product-path risk.

excluded: Do not claim full codebase coverage beyond the selected async/action path.

relationships: Trace click-handler -> async action -> lifecycle/state owner before concluding review coverage.
ambiguities: If product-path behavior was not validated end-to-end, report it as an explicit coverage gap.
knownExclusions: Do not treat changed-files-only review as sufficient evidence.
evidenceRequirements: Use concrete path:line evidence for the async action, caller context, state/lifecycle owner, and related tests.
doneWhen: Review output distinguishes directly reviewed files from connected context.
Connected context (caller/click-handler, lifecycle/state owner, related tests) is represented as discovered surfaces, not only coverage-note text.
Coverage notes include an explicit product-path validation gap when tests do not cover end-to-end behavior.

reviewPacket.goal: Challenge applicable adversarial failure-mode classes while respecting non-applicable packet boundaries.

notes: This scenario mirrors the missed soft-focus incident shape without depending on external provider APIs.
A capture must trace panel action timing through lifecycle/state owners; mentioning async/race keywords is insufficient.

reviewPacket.goal: Verify the review traces a panel click/action through deferred registration, scene lifecycle setup, and session/current-scene state commit behavior.

included: Async boundary: deferred registration / pending action in src/shell/sessionPanels.ts
Lifecycle owner: scene start/setup in src/scenes/PracticeScene.ts
State owner: session/current-scene store in src/game/navigation.ts

relationships: Trace panel click/action -> deferred registration/pending action -> scene start/setup -> session/current-scene commit before concluding review coverage.
Challenge whether stale first action can override later user intent after async registration resolves.
Challenge whether state commits before scene.start(...) throws are rolled back or recorded as a validation gap.
ambiguities: Existing rejection tests are insufficient if they do not prove concurrent interleaving and rollback semantics.
knownExclusions: Do not pass this scenario with only changed-files coverage or generic async/race terminology.
evidenceRequirements: Behavior checks must name the entrypoint, async boundary, lifecycle owner, state owner, failure path, and validation oracle or explicit gap.
Use concrete first-party path:line evidence for directly reviewed soft-focus surfaces.
doneWhen: The output includes behaviorChecks for async_event_ordering, lifecycle_reentrancy, state_commit_rollback, and test_oracle_authenticity.
Validation coverage explains why existing rejection tests do or do not prove concurrent interleaving and rollback.

requiredDirectReview: Lifecycle owner: scene start/setup in src/scenes/PracticeScene.ts
State owner: session/current-scene store in src/game/navigation.ts

requiredText: stale first action overrides later user intent
